title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Agent Decisions Reveal Implicit Biases in Language Models

live_model.evidence: Sec. 4: "we tested six LLMs -- GPT-3, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o..."; Sec. 5.3: "GPT-4-turbo...exhibited significant implicit biases in 9/12 cases, avg DPD 0.513"

prompt.location: Appendix Sections B and C (persona/action-generation prompts, implicit-bias test); Appendix Section D (explicit-bias question prompts)
prompt.note: Language-agent simulation: personas are generated then agents decide an action (e.g. evacuate/stay); DPD (demographic parity difference) is computed across sociodemographic attributes.

claim.metric: average demographic parity difference (DPD), implicit bias, GPT-4-turbo
claim.location: Sec. 5.3 ("GPT-4-turbo also exhibited significant implicit biases in 9 out of 12 cases, with an average DPD of 0.513 (sd = 0.373)"); n_items = 100 agent personas x 12 sociodemographic-group x scenario combinations (Sec. 4.1); detailed per-case results in Appendix Figs. 11-12

data.source: Self-contained: 4 scenarios (Emergency Response, Authority Compliance, Negative Info Sharing, Career Path) fully specified in paper/Appendix; no external dataset needed

notes: The paper also reports an explicit-bias DPD for GPT-4-turbo (0 out of 12 cases significant, average DPD=0, sd=0.001; n=3600 = 12 cases x 300 agents) as a companion headline number. GPT-4o (undated, co-primary focus model) is also tested but not resolved here since GPT-4-turbo already gives a clean eligible record; GPT-3 is used to help format GPT-3's own outputs via GPT-4o (utility role, not a separate claim). est_calls is a rough 3-seed-equivalent estimate for the implicit-bias condition alone (multi-stage pipeline: persona generation + action generation + rationale, so real per-item call count may be higher than 1).
